mainTopic: Where the rules come from for women being exempt from time-bound מצוות and obligated in non-time-bound ones, and how the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד protects those sources
overview: The גמרא has a rule, learned from תפילין, that women are exempt from מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא (positive מצוות tied to a set time). It first explains why the תורה still writes special exclusions for סוכה and ראייה: they block a גזירה שוה from מצה or from הקהל that would have obligated women. Next it asks why the rule is not learned from שמחה, where women are included, to obligate them. אביי answers that a woman's שמחה is the duty of her husband, or for a widow, of the people she lives with. The גמרא then asks why the rule is not learned from הקהל. It answers that מצה and הקהל are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, two verses teaching the same thing, so they cannot set a general rule. It shows that תפילין and ראייה are each needed, while women in הקהל already follows from the children, so the rule holds. It then asks what to say according to the opinion that such verses do teach, and adds a second difficulty. Women are obligated in non-time-bound מצוות, learned from מורא אב ואם, and תלמוד תורה and פריה ורביה cannot teach the opposite, because they are two verses that come as one. That question is taken up on the next amud.

steps.title: The special word for סוכה is needed to block a link to מצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that without a special exclusion, we might have linked סוכה to מצה through the shared words 'fifteenth day' and obligated women in סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: let us learn 'fifteenth' from 'fifteenth' written about the festival of מצות. Just as there women are obligated, so too here women are obligated. So the special word was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from just before this section: why does the תורה need a special word (האזרח) to exempt women from סוכה if they are already exempt from time-bound מצוות? It says the word blocks a mistaken comparison to מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both סוכות and פסח are described as starting on the 'fifteenth' day of the month. That shared word could create a גזירה שוה, and since women are obligated in מצה even though it is time-bound, we might have obligated them in סוכה too. The special exclusion stops that comparison, so the general rule of exemption stays in place for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (the pasuk is not extra)
You might have thought to say
Let us learn (derive)
Linking two topics through a shared word in the pesukim
Just as there ... so too here
It is necessary

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say women are obligated in סוכה. It explains why the תורה had to write a special exclusion: to stop a comparison to מצה that would otherwise have obligated them.

phrases.english: It was needed, for you might have thought to say:
Let us learn 'fifteenth' from 'fifteenth' written about the festival of מצות,
just as there women are obligated,
so too here women are obligated.
So it was necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about why סוכה needs its own exclusion of women.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is not extra; it blocks a possible גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have linked סוכה to מצה through the word 'fifteenth' and obligated women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special word exempts women from סוכה, keeping the general rule in force there.

steps.title: ראייה also has its own exclusion of women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: ראייה is time-bound, yet the תורה writes 'your males' to exclude women, which suggests that without it women would be obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is ראייה, which is a time-bound positive מצוה. The reason women are exempt is that the תורה wrote 'your males' to exclude women. This implies that otherwise women would be obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case, ראייה (appearing at the בית המקדש on the festivals), that seems to break the general rule. Why would the תורה need 'your males' if women are already exempt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women were automatically exempt from every time-bound מצוה, the word זכורך would be unneeded. Since the תורה wrote it, it seems that without it women would have been obligated, so the general rule looks weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of appearing at the בית המקדש on the festivals
A positive מצוה tied to a set time
The Merciful One (the תורה)
Your males
But if it were not so

phrases.english: But there is ראייה,
which is a positive מצוה tied to a set time,
and the reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'your males',
to exclude women;
but if not for this, women would be obligated!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי רְאִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second case with the same problem as סוכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule that women are exempt from all time-bound positive מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה's special exclusion for ראייה implies that, without it, women would be obligated, so the general rule seems not to apply automatically.

steps.title: The word for ראייה is needed to block a link to הקהל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without 'your males,' we might have learned ראייה from הקהל through the shared word 'appear,' and obligated women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: let us learn 'appearing' from 'appearing' written about הקהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as for סוכה. The word זכורך blocks a mistaken comparison to הקהל, where women are obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of הקהל also uses the word 'appear,' and women are obligated in הקהל. That shared word could create a גזירה שוה obligating women in ראייה. The תורה wrote זכורך to stop it, so the general rule stays intact.

keyTerms.meaning: The gathering of all Israel to hear the תורה read by the king
The shared word 'appear' that could link the two מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: In both סוכה and ראייה, the special exclusion of women is not extra. It blocks a גזירה שוה that would otherwise obligate them, so the general rule exempting women from time-bound מצוות still stands.

phrases.english: It was needed, for you might have thought to say:
Let us learn 'appearing' from 'appearing' written about הקהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: נֵילַף ״רְאִיָּה״ ״רְאִיָּה״ מֵהַקְהֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from ראייה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is not extra; it blocks a possible גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have linked ראייה to הקהל through the word 'appear' and obligated women.
steps.terutzMaskana: זכורך exempts women from ראייה, and the general rule remains.

steps.title: Why not learn from שמחה to obligate women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the general rule was learned from תפילין to exempt women, rather than from שמחה, a time-bound מצוה where women are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before learning from תפילין to exempt women, let us learn from שמחה to obligate them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main source of the general rule. It asks why we chose תפילין, where women are exempt, as the model, instead of שמחה on יום טוב, where women seem obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמחה on יום טוב is also time-bound, and women are included in it. So there seem to be two possible models pulling in opposite directions. The question is why the exempting model of תפילין wins.

keyTerms.meaning: And before we learn
תפילין, the earlier source for exempting women
To exempt
The מצוה of rejoicing on יום טוב
To obligate

phrases.english: And before we learn from תפילין to exempt,
phrases.notes: Earlier on this daf the general exemption for women was learned from תפילין.

phrases.english: let us learn from rejoicing to obligate!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַדְּיָלְפִינַן מִתְּפִילִּין לִפְטוּרָא, נֵילַף מִשִּׂמְחָה לְחִיּוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from specific exclusions back to challenging the main source of the general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing תפילין as the model for all time-bound positive מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמחה is also time-bound and women are included, so it could serve as a model to obligate women instead.

steps.title: אביי: a woman's שמחה is her husband's job
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that women are not directly obligated in שמחה; the husband is obligated to make his wife happy, so שמחה cannot be a model for obligating women.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A woman, her husband makes her happy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. שמחה cannot show that women are obligated in time-bound מצוות, because the מצוה is on the husband to make his wife happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed women themselves carry the מצוה of שמחה. אביי says the obligation sits on the husband, and the wife is the one being made happy. So שמחה is not a real example of a woman's own obligation, and תפילין stays the model.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, an אמורא
Her husband makes her happy

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule exempting women from time-bound positive מצוות is learned from תפילין. שמחה does not challenge it, because the מצוה of a woman's שמחה is on her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This protects the main source of the general rule exempting women from מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא.

phrases.english: אביי said:
A woman, her husband makes her happy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִשָּׁה בַּעֲלָהּ מְשַׂמְּחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from שמחה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women themselves are obligated in שמחה, so it could be a model to obligate them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband carries the obligation to make his wife happy, so שמחה is no model and תפילין remains the source.

steps.title: What about a widow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if שמחה is really the husband's duty, how does that work for a widow, who has no husband?
steps.simpleTranslation: What can be said about a widow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's answer. A widow has no husband, yet the תורה includes her in the מצוה of rejoicing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said women are not directly obligated in שמחה, because the husband must make his wife happy. A widow has no husband, so it looks like she must be obligated herself. If so, שמחה would again be a time-bound מצוה that women are obligated in.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: A widow, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The widow is listed among those who rejoice on the יום טוב in דברים 16:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that women's שמחה is only the husband's obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow has no husband, yet she is included in שמחה, so the obligation seems to fall on her directly.

steps.title: The obligation is on the people she lives with
steps.stepSummary: The duty to make a widow happy falls on the people she is living with.
steps.simpleTranslation: It applies to the one with whom she is staying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even for a widow, the מצוה is on someone else: the person whose household she lives in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model stays the same. Someone else is responsible for the woman's joy, whether that is a husband or a host. So שמחה still cannot be used as a model for women being directly obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying, dwelling
With him, by him

phrases.english: With the one with whom she is staying.
phrases.notes: Meaning: the obligation is on the man whose home she lives in, not on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁרוּיָה אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the widow challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the same principle to a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A widow must be directly obligated in שמחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The people she lives with are obligated to make her happy, so שמחה still does not directly obligate women.

steps.title: Why not learn from הקהל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: women are obligated in הקהל, a time-bound מצוה, so why not learn from it that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from הקהל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new possible model: הקהל, where the תורה clearly includes women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמחה was rejected as a model. But הקהל is a time-bound מצוה, and women are clearly obligated in it. So why not use it as the general rule, instead of תפילין?

keyTerms.meaning: The gathering of the nation every seven years to hear the king read the תורה
Let us learn (derive)

phrases.english: But let us learn from the gathering (הקהל)!
phrases.notes: In הקהל women are named explicitly; see דברים 31:12.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מֵהַקְהֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמחה is ruled out, the גמרא offers another model in its place.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of תפילין as the model for the general rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקהל is a time-bound מצוה that obligates women, so it could serve as the model for obligating women in all such מצוות.

steps.title: מצה and הקהל are two verses teaching the same thing
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from הקהל, because מצה and הקהל both teach that women are obligated. Two verses that teach the same thing do not set a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because מצה and הקהל are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using a known rule. When two פסוקים teach the same idea, we treat them as special exceptions, not as a model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had wanted women obligated in every time-bound מצוה, one example would have been enough. Writing it twice, for מצה and for הקהל, shows that these are exceptions. So neither one can teach a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that come as one: two פסוקים teaching the same idea
They do not teach (cannot be used as a model for other cases)
The מצוה of eating מצה on פסח

steps.whatToRemember: When the תורה teaches the same rule in two places, those cases are exceptions and cannot be expanded to others.

phrases.english: Because מצה and הקהל are
two verses that come as one,
phrases.notes: Both teach the same thing: women are obligated even though these מצוות are time-bound.

phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה מַצָּה וְהַקְהֵל שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הקהל challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הקהל could be the model for obligating women in all time-bound מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: מצה and הקהל are two verses teaching the same thing, so they are exceptions and teach nothing beyond themselves.

steps.title: תפילין and ראייה are also two verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same rule around: תפילין and ראייה both exempt women, so they should also be two verses that come as one and teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תפילין and ראייה are also two verses that come as one, and they should not teach!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the rule it just applied to attack the source for the exemption itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two verses teaching the same thing cannot set a rule, the exemption has the same problem. Both תפילין and ראייה exempt women. Then תפילין should not be able to teach that women are exempt from all time-bound מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The מצוה of appearing at the בית המקדש on the רגלים

phrases.english: If so, תפילין and appearance (ראייה) are also
two verses that come as one
and they do not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, תְּפִילִּין וּרְאִיָּה נָמֵי שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the principle from Step 9 against the exemption derived from תפילין.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using תפילין as the source for exempting women from all time-bound מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין and ראייה both teach the exemption, so by the same rule neither should serve as a general model.

steps.title: Both are needed: without ראייה we would learn from הקהל
steps.stepSummary: The two verses are each needed. If the תורה had written only תפילין, we would have obligated women in ראייה through the shared word 'appear' in הקהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are both needed. If the תורה had written תפילין and not ראייה, I would have said: let us learn 'appearance' from 'appearance' in הקהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule of two verses only applies when the second verse is extra. Here each verse is needed for its own reason. This step explains why ראייה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without its own exclusion, ראייה would have been linked to הקהל through the shared word 'appear', and women would have been obligated. That link would beat the general rule from תפילין. So the תורה had to exclude women from ראייה separately (as in Step 3).

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (each verse teaches something the other could not)
I would have said (the mistaken assumption)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Needed' does not mean the exemption is weaker. It means each פסוק blocks a different mistake, so they are not a repeat, and תפילין can still teach the general rule.

phrases.english: They are needed, for if the Merciful One had written תפילין
and had not written appearance,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: נֵילַף רְאִיָּה רְאִיָּה מֵהַקְהֵל.
phrases.english: I would have said: let us learn 'appearance' from 'appearance' of הקהל.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא תְּפִילִּין וְלָא כְּתַב רְאִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 10 by showing the ראייה verse is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without its own verse, ראייה would be learned from הקהל and women would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ראייה verse is needed to block that link, so it is not a repeat of תפילין.

steps.title: Without תפילין we would compare it to מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only ראייה, we would have compared תפילין to מזוזה and obligated women. So both verses are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written ראייה and not תפילין, I would have said: compare תפילין to מזוזה. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing why the תפילין verse is also needed. This closes the challenge from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without its own exclusion, תפילין would be compared to מזוזה, where women are obligated. So the תורה had to exclude women from תפילין separately. Since each verse is needed, they are not two verses that come as one, and תפילין can serve as the model for exempting women.

keyTerms.meaning: I will compare (link two מצוות placed side by side)
The scroll on the doorpost
It is needed (closing the answer)

steps.whatToRemember: תפילין and ראייה each block a different mistaken link (ראייה from הקהל, תפילין from מזוזה). So they are not a repeat, and the rule that women are exempt from time-bound מצוות stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This protects the source for the general rule that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written appearance
and had not written תפילין,
I would have said: I will compare תפילין to מזוזה,
phrases.notes: תפילין and מזוזה sit right next to each other in the פסוקים, and women are obligated in מזוזה.

phrases.english: It is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא רְאִיָּה וְלָא כְּתַב תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 11 by showing the תפילין verse is also needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without its own verse, תפילין would be compared to מזוזה and women would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, so they are not 'two verses that come as one', and תפילין can teach the general exemption.

steps.title: Maybe מצה and הקהל are also each needed
steps.stepSummary: Using the same reasoning as steps 11–12, the גמרא suggests that מצה and הקהל are each needed, so they should not count as two verses teaching one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then מצה and הקהל should also both be needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reply it just gave for תפילין and ראייה and applies it to מצה and הקהל. If each of those is needed too, then we could learn a general rule from them after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, מצה and הקהל were set aside because they repeat the same lesson. Now the גמרא says: maybe each verse has its own job, just like תפילין and ראייה. If so, they are not 'two verses as one', and the source for obligating women would come back.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that reasoning is correct
Also
They are needed; each verse has its own purpose
The מצוה of eating matza on פסח
The gathering of the nation to hear the תורה read after שמיטה

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If you explain that each verse is needed, the way you did for תפילין and ראייה.

phrases.english: matza and assembly are also necessary!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַצָּה וְהַקְהֵל נָמֵי צְרִיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the 'both are needed' reply from steps 11–12 back against the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that מצה and הקהל are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'each verse is needed' saves תפילין and ראייה, the same idea should save מצה and הקהל, which would bring back their power to teach.

steps.title: מצה is needed so we don't learn from סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that the verse about מצה is needed. Without it, we would compare פסח to סוכות through the shared words 'fifteenth' and exempt women from מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would both be needed? Granted, if the תורה had written only הקהל and not מצה, I would have said: let us learn 'fifteenth' and 'fifteenth' from the festival of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by checking each verse. Here it agrees that the מצה verse really is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסח and סוכות are called 'the fifteenth' day of the month. Women are exempt from סוכה, so without a verse we would have exempted them from מצה too. That is why the תורה had to state that women eat מצה. The real test, which comes in the next step, is whether הקהל is also needed.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose?
Granted; this part makes sense
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have thought
Let us learn or derive

phrases.english: For what are they needed?
Granted, if the Merciful One had written assembly
and had not written matza,
I would have said:
Let us derive 'fifteenth' and 'fifteenth'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:6 for פסח and ויקרא 23:34 for סוכות. Both use the word 'fifteenth'.

phrases.english: from the festival of Sukkot.
phrases.notes: Women are exempt from סוכה, so we would have exempted them from מצה too.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי צְרִיכִי? בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא הַקְהֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 13 by agreeing that the first of the two verses, מצה, is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession: one of the two verses is shown to be needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the מצה verse, we would compare פסח to סוכות and exempt women from מצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצה verse is needed. Whether הקהל is needed is checked next.

steps.title: הקהל is not needed, so the two verses still teach nothing
steps.stepSummary: The verse about women in הקהל is not needed, because if children must come, women surely must come. So מצה and הקהל stay as two verses that come as one and teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תורה could have written only מצה, and הקהל would not be needed. I would have said on my own: if children are obligated, surely women are! Therefore they are two verses that come as one, and they do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows that the הקהל verse about women is extra, so step 9's answer stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse of הקהל says children must come. From that, a קל וחומר already tells us women must come. Since the תורה still wrote 'women' anyway, the two verses really are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, unlike תפילין and ראייה, where each verse was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Young children
All the more so; a קל וחומר
Therefore
Two verses that come as one, teaching the same thing
They do not teach a general rule

steps.whatToRemember: מצה is needed so we don't learn from סוכות, but women in הקהל is obvious from children. So מצה and הקהל are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, and they cannot teach that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the הקהל verse is useless for children. Only the mention of women is extra, since it follows from the children.

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write matza,
and assembly would not be needed,
and I would say:
Children are obligated,
women, all the more so!
Therefore, they are
two verses that come as one,
and they do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא מַצָּה, וְלָא בָּעֵי הַקְהֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 14 by showing that the second verse, הקהל, is extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows one verse is extra, so the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד still applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe מצה and הקהל are each needed, like תפילין and ראייה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mention of women in הקהל follows from a קל וחומר from children, so the two verses teach nothing.

steps.title: What about the opinion that two such verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 9 only works for the opinion that two verses coming as one do not teach. According to the opinion that they do teach, the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says they do not teach. But according to the one who says they do teach, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that its whole answer depends on one side of a disagreement. It challenges the answer from the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about whether שני כתובים הבאים כאחד can teach a general rule. If they can, then מצה and הקהל should teach that women are obligated in all time-bound מצוות, and step 8's question comes back. The גמרא does not answer yet. With וְתוּ in the next step it adds a second difficulty, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
According to the one who says
They do teach a general rule
What can be said? (there seems to be no answer)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says they do not teach,
but according to the one who says they do teach,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that was just secured in steps 9–15 by pointing to a competing opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that מצה and הקהל cannot teach because they are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer depends on the view that such verses do not teach. According to the view that they do teach, מצה and הקהל should obligate women in all time-bound מצוות.

steps.title: Where do we learn women are obligated in non-time-bound מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a further question: what is the source that women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: positive מצוות that are not time-bound, from where do we know that women are obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'and furthermore' signals that the גמרא is adding another difficulty. It starts by asking for the source of a basic rule, setting up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about time-bound מצוות. Now the גמרא asks about the other side: מצוות that are not time-bound. The source it finds will soon raise a problem of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; another question
A positive commandment, something you must do
Not caused by time; not tied to a specific time
From where do we know?

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
phrases.english: And furthermore: a positive מצוה that is not time-bound,
from where do we know that women are obligated?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ נָשִׁים חַיָּיבוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new line of difficulty after step 16's open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound.

steps.title: We learn it from מורא אב ואם
steps.stepSummary: The source is מורא, fearing one's parents. Women are obligated in it, so they are obligated in every positive מצוה that is not time-bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from fear of parents: just as women are obligated in fearing parents, so too women are obligated in every positive מצוה that is not time-bound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17 by pointing to מורא אב ואם as the model case. This answer is the setup for the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מורא is a positive מצוה not tied to time, and women are obligated in it. From this one case, the גמרא builds a general rule for all similar מצוות. The comparison 'just as… so too' uses one case as a model for a whole group, and that will matter for the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Because one derives or learns
Fear or reverence of one's father and mother
Just as… so too; learning a group from one model case

steps.whyThisMatters: A single model case is now being used to build a general rule for women. This opens the door to asking why a different single case, תלמוד תורה, where women are exempt, could not build the opposite rule.

phrases.english: For one derives it from fear,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3: 'Each man shall fear his mother and his father.'

phrases.english: just as with fear, women are obligated,
so too every positive מצוה
that is not time-bound, women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָלֵיף מִמּוֹרָא, מָה מוֹרָא נָשִׁים חַיָּיבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and sets up the next challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women's obligation in non-time-bound positive מצוות is learned from מורא אב ואם, using a 'just as… so too' comparison.

steps.title: Why not learn the opposite from תלמוד תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source from מורא: women are exempt from תלמוד תורה, which is not time-bound, so why not learn from it that women are exempt from all non-time-bound positive מצוות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from תלמוד תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 18. It suggests a different model, תלמוד תורה, that would lead to the opposite rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תלמוד תורה is a positive מצוה that is not time-bound, yet women are exempt from it. If we copy that case, women would be exempt from every non-time-bound positive מצוה. So why choose מורא as the model and not תלמוד תורה?

keyTerms.meaning: and let us learn / derive
the מצוה of Torah study

phrases.english: But let us learn from Torah study!
phrases.notes: The idea: women are exempt from Torah study even though it is not time-bound, so maybe they are exempt from all such מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מִתַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 18 by offering a competing model that points the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that מורא is the model for all non-time-bound positive מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a competing model, תלמוד תורה, where women are exempt from a non-time-bound מצוה. That could teach the opposite general rule.

steps.title: תלמוד תורה and פריה ורביה are two verses that do not teach
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from תלמוד תורה, because it and פריה ורביה are two verses teaching the same exemption, and two verses that come as one do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תלמוד תורה and פריה ורביה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19. It explains why תלמוד תורה cannot be the model for other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are also exempt from פריה ורביה, another non-time-bound מצוה. If the תורה had to tell us this exemption twice, the message is that these are special exceptions, not a pattern to copy. So מורא stays as the model, and women are obligated in non-time-bound positive מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה to have children
two verses that teach the same point
they do not teach (a general rule for other cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound, learned from מורא. תלמוד תורה and פריה ורביה are exceptions, because two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean women's exemption from תלמוד תורה or פריה ורביה is doubtful. Those exemptions stand. They just cannot be stretched into a general rule.

phrases.english: Because we have Torah study
and the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply,
phrases.notes: Women are exempt from this one too, even though it is not time-bound.

phrases.english: two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה וּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and keeps step 18's source in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Blocks the competing model by applying the rule that two verses coming as one do not teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought תלמוד תורה shows that women are exempt from all non-time-bound positive מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: תלמוד תורה and פריה ורביה are two parallel exemptions, so they are exceptions that teach nothing. מורא remains the model, and women are obligated.
